newsitem.title: UK: Hogg sees difficulties in relaxing EU beef ban.
newsitem.headline: Hogg sees difficulties in relaxing EU beef ban.

text.p: Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg admitted on Tuesday it would be difficult to persuade the European Union to lift a ban it imposed on British beef exports in March over fears of mad cow disease spreading to humans.

Hogg announced on Monday that Britain would go ahead with an additional selective cull of cattle most at risk of contracting mad cow disease, or BSE, in an effort to get the EU to agree to a phased lifting of the ban. This would start with so-called certified herds guaranteed to be free of BSE.
But asked by BBC radio how quickly progress could be made, Hogg said: "I think it is going to be difficult."
Hogg was speaking from Brussels where he is to meet fellow EU farm ministers later on Tuesday.
He said Britian would present detailed proposals aimed at lifting the ban on exports from certified herds in late January or early February following consultations with farmers.

The government had established a framework for making progress in line with the agreement reached by EU leaders at their Florence summit in June and the ball was now in the court of the EU, the minister said.

Asked for his views on an editorial in the Daily Telegraph, which said government capitulation in the beef war had been accompanied by defiant rhetoric, Hogg said: "I hope we will get steady, step-by-step progress.
"It's going to be slow, it's going to be less fast than we would wish, and there'll be difficult negotiations. But I hope that we will make progress, and I believe we will make some."
